title: 3d hack and slash. 2 weeks with claude
author: Boring-Dot104
selftext:
i was really scared to post this since it's very unpolished, but i also couldn't hold it in anymore. i'm really excited to finally show this very ambitious project.

i'm about 2 weeks in, still a ton to do like more attacks, hit effects, and proper sound.

imo souls combat felt too slow, and dmc/bayonetta is a bit too fast (though i haven’t played them for long <1hr). i wanted to find a nice in-between without losing my own direction. a lot of games feel good to play but are missing deeper systems for customization and player agency, especially with a bit of roguelike rng mixed in.

for background, i mostly play league and fighting games. growing up i played stuff like dynasty warriors, mega man, mario, and final fantasy. i have pretty minimal unity experience—spent some time in tutorial hell so i know my way around a bit.

this started from an old project where i could just move and swing a sword with an animation, no real functionality. i grabbed a bunch of assets i owned and picked up some more on sale (ty ida faber and magic pig games), then used claude to help iterate, constantly planning and prompting. claude gave me directions and ideas based off of my vision that i described. been working on it every day for the past 2 weeks.

while it looks crappy and plain, there were many hidden systems in that may not have been caught, but also there is a gear/shop system (affix re-rolls, stat upgrade):  
[https://streamable.com/7rnwl6](https://streamable.com/7rnwl6)  
dragon dies in like 5 hits when i wear the best gear. also lmao @ the shopkeeper

anyways, i hope you guys like how it's looking so far. i'm aiming to improve every small thing x10 once the core feels solid. the goal is to turn this into a roguelike with different weapon sets, playstyles, and eventually multiplayer to enjoy with friends. currently doing more planning with claude and then finally finishing the implement on air combos then add a skills/stamina resource economy.

i'll try to post more updates soon! feedback or support in any form means a lot, thank you so much. : )

comments.author: RecordingTechnical86
comments.body: Looks very nice. Did you use asset and animation packs? Do you already have a usp or story in mind?

replies.author: Boring-Dot104
replies.body:
thank you. yes, all different packs were used. while i do have licenses to use them, i dont know if they'll make it to the final product. i have some friends who can do commissions, but that takes time and money.   
  
this is my take on fun, fast-paced combat. when im stressed out from pvp-centric games but want to keep high-intensity, hopefully this game can still scratch the itch.

replies.author: Living_Advice_1225
replies.body: How does Claude help? Just writing the code? The rest of the UI work like creating objects and setting materials are done manually?

replies.author: Boring-Dot104
replies.body: it does code- it helps a lot to know what you want, whether you do or don't, talk with it and plan before executing. it also gives suggestions to supplement the direction of your design. id say just check it out and see, it's pretty good. a lot of stuff doesn't land in the first pass and if it does, it can be a bit "lifeless" so you have to constantly iterate and tweak the feel which is why i move on to the next feature after working proof of concept. settings and parameters it does do, UI stuff- is like 75% you, but it tells you the steps of where you gotta click.

replies.author: reverendblueball
replies.body:
A tech stack is the collection of technologies you use to create your app/game/website.

For instance, I saw that you used Unity/Claude. This could be your complete stack.

But your complete stack could be Krita for design, Godot for the game engine, Gemini Pro to help with development, and Dialogic for conversations between characters.
